findings.reason: an orchestrator sizing §11 from the roadmap sees no dependency and can dispatch it before the cutover the section says it must wait for.
findings.text: plan-depends-on declares only `flux-function-forward-equilibrium`, but §5's gate-state note ("waits on single-grid-solver-cutover", line 777 also states it) and §11's done-when ("queued as the first node after single-grid-solver-cutover lands", line 373) both make the plan's live sections depend on `single-grid-solver-cutover` landing first; that plan declares `plan-blocks="efit-baseline-demonstration"` and does not block this one, so the dependency exists in prose but in neither plan's relationship fields

findings.reason: the declared measure is not the measure the section was authored against, so a re-open would re-apply an inapplicable bar.
findings.text: §2's done-when still reads "reproduces the challenge starter-kit vacuum check (reported R²≈0.94 class)", but decision `vacuum-gate-measure` (line 406) records that the published 0.94 scores a *fitted* exterior decomposition and "the gate as written cannot pass or fail the entry premise", replacing it with the plasma-subtraction differencing measure whose preregistered bar is 0.4952670786; the section passed on the replacement (per-frame R² quartiles 0.99325/0.99908/0.99967), not on the 0.94 line the done-when still names

findings.reason: §5 is a live, buildable section, and a node reading only the done-when would score against a floor the forward-operator-refinement adjudication returned NO_DEFENSIBLE_DIIID_TOLERANCE_DERIVED for.
findings.text: §5's done-when measures "extracted flux functions re-solve to the labeled map at the grid-resolution floor", but the section's own gate-state note at line 164 states that "the 'grid-resolution floor' phrasing in the done-when below is superseded by f-dfo-004's re-scope to the label-representability ceiling (median interior R² 0.949)", and f-dfo-004's body confirms the bar is set relative to that ceiling; the docu-when was left carrying the superseded text

findings.reason: both halves are assertions about one criterion's provenance and the node closes on one verdict, but the two measures are independent enough that a reviewer should read them separately; flagging so the author can split if desired rather than as a blocking defect.
findings.text: §11 states two deliverables in one node: "Build the estimator the forward-operator-reflecting adjudication asked for" and, "In the same node, repair the pin in `benchmarks/diiid_forward_gs_match.py`: `GATE_RESIDUAL_TOLERANCE` is 1.0e-6 … and must either read the registered value or carry its derivation", with both surfacing in the done-when ("the estimator reproduces an analytic fixture's known error order" and "the gate constant matches its registration")

findings.reason: the file is a retired follow-on reference in a landed comment; §11 and the live sections do not cite it, so no node acts on the dead pointer.
findings.text: comment `c-20260823T1012-repaired-ring` names `benchmarks/diiid_machine_ids_export.py` as the owner of an orphaned 82-vertex assertion a cleanup node will retire, but no file of that name exists in the tree (only `benchmarks/diiid_ids_machine_description.py` and `benchmarks/diiid_machine_description.py`), so the pointer no longer resolves

findings.reason: a node following §11 literally could retain the un-derived constant the cited correction says must be restored, changing the gate's outcome for every future run.
findings.text: §11 instructs that the gate constant "must either read the registered value or carry its derivation", but the comment it cites as its source (`c-20260823T0935-criterion-correction`, the "2026-08-23 criterion-correction comment") records that "the re-evaluation run must apply the REGISTERED tolerance — restoring the gate as registered, not moving it"; the "or carry its derivation" escape permits keeping the untraced 1.0e-6, which is the opposite of the correction the text grounds itself on

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the retired followup pointer `benchmarks/diiid_machine_ids_export.py` no longer resolves; all other cited modules, symbols, plans, decision keys and archive anchors resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — two done-whens (§2, §5) still name bars that the plan's own later decisions replaced, so a node reading the done-when line applies a superseded measure.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every artifact in `plan-artifacts` is a durable path (`docs/figures/...` in git, or a `/work/projects/imas_gpu/...` GPFS pointer); no session scratchpad path is asserted as a record location.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §11 introduces no new symbol or filename, and the symbols it names (`_fit_held_out_ladder`, `_fit_power_order`, `richardson_fine_error`, `GATE_RESIDUAL_TOLERANCE`) are existing mechanism-describing identifiers, not plan labels.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §11's instruction that the gate constant "must either read the registered value or carry its derivation" contradicts the 2026-08-23 criterion-correction comment it cites, which requires the registered value be restored.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §11 bundles two deliverables, an estimator build and a gate-constant repair, behind one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5's gate and §11's post-cutover run both require `single-grid-solver-cutover` to land, yet `plan-depends-on` declares only `flux-function-forward-equilibrium`.
